description: MVBench is a comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging temporal video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. It uses a static-to-dynamic method to define temporal tasks, and automatically converts public video annotations into multiple-choice QA pairs for evaluating Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). The benchmark covers tasks ranging from perception to cognition, sourced from 11 public video datasets.
name: MVBench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The benchmark uses ground-truth video annotations from public datasets to guarantee evaluation fairness and accuracy, avoiding biased scoring of LLMs. The answer prompt "Best Option: (" achieves a 100% option extraction rate, compared to 87% alignment rate with humans for ChatGPT-based extraction methods.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: QA pairs are automatically generated from public video annotations. Two approaches are used: (1) Template-Based Construction: option candidates are constructed directly from ground truth annotations; (2) LLM-Based Generation: ChatGPT is used to generate questions based on task definitions and to convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format. 200 multiple-choice QA pairs are produced per task. Answer options are randomly sampled (3–5 per question), shuffled, and length-balanced using LLM.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark avoids biased scoring by using ground-truth video annotations rather than LLM-based scoring of open-ended answers. The multiple-choice format is used specifically to prevent evaluation bias from LLMs or user studies. Answer option length bias is mitigated by using LLM to ensure all options have similar and reasonable lengths.
rai:dataCollection: Videos are selected from 11 existing public video benchmarks (STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, TVQA). Videos are filtered for diversity, temporal sensitivity (duration primarily 5s–35s), and question difficulty. Multiple-choice QA pairs are automatically generated from the video annotations using ChatGPT and template-based methods.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos and annotations from 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1 (MiT V1), FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. These cover real-world and simulated environments, indoor and outdoor scenes, and first-person and third-person perspectives.
rai:dataLimitations: There is a minimal source gap between the instruction data and MVBench: CLEVRER in the instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference tasks, and Action Antonym videos are from SthSthV2 while antonyms are from PAXION, making evaluation not strictly out-domain. Current MLLMs struggle with position, count, and character tasks. Visual information alone may be insufficient for cognition tasks like egocentric navigation and episodic reasoning.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For STAR, the challenge is enhanced by randomly shifting the start or end points of video clips. For CLEVRER, questions requiring more than 10 conditions are excluded. Answer options are randomly sampled (3–5 per question) and shuffled. For Moving Count, the original answer is randomly shifted to create distractors.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtration includes: (1) selecting videos with intermediate duration (primarily 5s–35s) to ensure temporal sensitivity; (2) filtering for question difficulty (e.g., for STAR, randomly shifting start/end points; for CLEVRER, excluding questions requiring more than 10 conditions); (3) answer option processing: randomly sampling 3–5 options, shuffling option order, and using LLM to ensure similar and reasonable option lengths.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MVBench enables comprehensive evaluation of temporal understanding in MLLMs, revealing that existing state-of-the-art models are far from satisfactory in temporal understanding. It provides a path toward general video understanding and motivates development of stronger video MLLMs.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in the open world, covering 20 challenging video tasks from perception to cognition including action, object, position, scene, count, attribute, pose, character, and cognition tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT is used to generate questions and convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format. UMT-L/16 model is used to generate top-6 action predictions as answer candidates for the Fine-grained Action task.

evidence.description: we introduce a comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Bench mark, namely MVBench, which covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. Specifically, we first introduce a novel static-to-dynamic method to define these temporal-related tasks. By transforming various static tasks into dynamic ones, we enable the systematic generation of video tasks that require a broad spectrum of temporal skills, ranging from perception to cognition.

evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: The extensive results on our MVBench reveal that, the existing MLLMs are far from satisfactory in temporal understanding, while our VideoChat2 largely surpasses these leading models by over 15% on MVBench.
